newsitem.title: BULGARIA: High foreign currency demand presses Bulgaria lev.
newsitem.headline: High foreign currency demand presses Bulgaria lev.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev fell to 236.80-237 per dollar from 236 at the opening and 234 at Friday's close as foreign currency demand continued to outweigh supply on the interbank market, dealers said.
"(Foreign currency) supply is rather low, and dollars are bid at increasingly high exchange rates," one dealer said.
Dollar bids rose to 236.60/80 levs around 1130 local time (0830 GMT) from 235.50/236 in early trade while asks surged to 237.95-237.60.
The central bank sold small amounts of dollars near 236 levs in a bid to slow the lev's fall, commercial banks dealers said. Central bank officials declined comment.
Many banks are gripped by a severe lev shortage, which deters them from going long dollars and should prevent a further lev fall, traders said.
Pressure on the lev also rose on the cash market as more people rushed to convert levs into foreign currency before some expected new bank closures, traders said.
"People' confidence in banks has almost disappeared, and they exchange every single lev into foreign currency," another dealer said.

Central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov told Reuter Financial Television last week the central bank might seek the closure of more local banks as part of long delayed financial stabilisation programme. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
